items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: Stan Kenton did a show from the Palladium... he was going to hire a piano player for that, to play the band numbers. And they called me to do that.

ctx.x: Did you have any idea that you’d be making a thirty-some year career out of that?

No. Let me think. We got back after, eventually well I got that, well I guess “The Judy Canova Show.” Well see I was married by then and that made a difference. You know I didn’t want to be traveling around either, we had a child and so that started to sound good to me, and especially gosh, all these great guys from the swing bands were in the studios and the radio orchestras and movie studios. And I was talking about Burrows and that band, Vince Terry was the guitar player, I don’t know if you know any of these…

band, so he was going to conduct, and he was going to hire a piano player for that, to play the band numbers. And they called me to do that. And I think Shelly Manne was in the band, and I forgot the trombone player. But I looked up to these guys, like that’s the top of the world, you know, Stan Kenton’s band. And that’s when he was very big. And of course you know Shelly Manne was like winning Down Beat polls and all. And they were coming up to me and like thinking how great it was that I was in the studios see?…
